product_overview: SIR-Net Lab is an interactive lab for epidemic-style malware spread simulation on computer networks. It lets users explore deterministic compartmental models, stochastic graph propagation, mitigation strategies, calibration, sensitivity analysis, and mathematical theory through a browser-based interface.
core_goals: Simulate epidemic and malware spread using compartmental ODE models
Explore stochastic malware propagation across network topologies
Test containment strategies such as pulse patching, quarantine, and segmentation
Calibrate model parameters against outbreak data
Analyze parameter sensitivity and study the underlying epidemiological theory
Switch between light and dark themes for comfortable viewing

features.name: Dark Mode and Theme Switching
features.description: Allows users to switch between light and dark visual themes and keep the preferred appearance across visits.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Switch the theme setting -> Observe the interface change appearance immediately -> Reload the page -> See the preferred theme remain active

features.name: Epidemic ODE Simulator
features.description: Lets users configure compartmental epidemic models and compare numerical solvers while viewing disease dynamics over time.
user_flows: Navigate to /simulator -> Adjust the transmission rate -> Adjust the recovery rate -> Select a numerical solver -> View the population curves and reproduction number update
Navigate to /simulator -> Choose a different compartmental model -> Adjust model parameters -> Select another solver -> Compare the resulting epidemic trajectory with the previous run

features.name: Network Topology Infection
features.description: Simulates malware spread over generated network topologies and lets users observe infected clusters as the simulation advances.
user_flows: Navigate to /network -> Select a network topology -> Set the number of nodes -> Set the edge probability -> Start the spread simulation -> Observe infection moving through the graph step by step
Navigate to /network -> Select another topology -> Change network size settings -> Advance the simulation again -> Inspect the changing infected clusters on the canvas

features.name: Intervention and Patching Control
features.description: Allows users to test mitigation strategies such as pulse patching and quarantine thresholds to reduce outbreak impact.
user_flows: Navigate to /control -> Configure the patching pulse schedule -> Adjust the quarantine threshold -> Run the simulation -> Compare the reduction in peak infection
Navigate to /control -> Modify the intervention timing -> Change the control settings -> Run the scenario again -> Observe how the outbreak response changes

features.name: Parameter Calibration
features.description: Lets users fit model parameters to outbreak data and review the estimated values and residuals.
user_flows: Navigate to /calibration -> Load the synthetic malware outbreak dataset -> Run parameter optimization -> View the estimated beta and gamma values -> Review the residual error summary
Navigate to /calibration -> Load a different dataset -> Run optimization again -> Compare the new fitted parameters with the previous results

features.name: Mathematical Theory and Formulas
features.description: Provides a browsable reference for SIR, SEIR, and SEIS models with rendered mathematical equations.
user_flows: Navigate to /theory -> Open the SIR section -> Open the SEIR section -> Open the SEIS section -> Inspect the rendered equations for each model
Navigate to /theory -> Browse the theory sections -> Read the mathematical definitions -> Compare the model formulations and thresholds

features.name: Interactive Containment Challenge
features.description: Presents a gamified containment scenario where users allocate limited resources to stop malware propagation and review the outcome.
user_flows: Navigate to /challenge -> Allocate budget across antivirus, network segmentation, and user awareness -> Trigger the malware outbreak scenario -> Review the resulting score and survival metrics
Navigate to /challenge -> Rebalance the resource allocation -> Start the scenario again -> Compare the new containment outcome with the previous attempt

features.name: About and GitHub Links
features.description: Shows project details, team information, and links to the repository.
user_flows: Navigate to /about -> Read the course and team information -> Follow the GitHub link -> View the repository page

features.name: UI Kit and Design System Showcase
features.description: Displays the design system tokens and interactive UI components used by the application.
user_flows: Navigate to /ui-kit -> Explore the design tokens -> Interact with the showcased components -> Observe the component states and accessibility behavior

routes.description: Landing page and overview of SIR-Net Lab
Deterministic epidemic ODE simulation (SIR, SEIR, SEIS) with Euler, RK4, and DOPRI5 solvers
Agent-based network epidemic propagation with d3-force graph visualization
Intervention strategies, pulse patching, quarantine, and threshold analysis
Model calibration and parameter fitting against historical or synthetic malware outbreak data
Global and local sensitivity analysis (Sobol / Morris) for epidemiological parameters
Mathematical reference and derivation of epidemiological models rendered with KaTeX
Interactive cybersecurity challenge for containment under budget constraints
Project information, academic references, team, and repository links
Component design system showcase with tokens and accessible interactive widgets
